summary: Our team Exon developed a project based on "Field Shift:Adapting Farms with NASA Data"; which will help farmer to save their crops from withering landslides, floods, droughts etc. and it will give plans for non-farmers on how to take care of specific crops and also provide good plans for crop rotation.
details:
Orbit Crop is a web application for farm planning and early warning. Orbit Crop helps farmers look at field conditions compare crop choices plan crop rotations and get ready for weather danger. A farmer can type in coordinates use GPS or search for a location and then draw a boundary around a field. Orbit Crop mixes that location with NASA climate information and other public data to give soil and moisture reports, estimates of which crops fit best advice on rotations and warnings about dangers such as heavy rain, flooding, heat, drought and strong wind.

The project brings types of information together into a useful workflow. NASA POWER supplies data on rainfall, temperature, sunlight and wetness. NASA GIBS offers a MODIS Terra NDVI map layer and NASA EONET adds reports of nearby natural events. Open‑Meteo gives forecasts, soil‑moisture estimates at depths and flood model data. SoilGrids and OpenLandMap supply modeled soil characteristics. Orbit Crop turns all of this input into comparisons of crops, seasonal planning views and recommended actions. It shows when a data source can not be reached.

Our aim is to make environmental information easier to reach and more helpful for farmers, especially where local monitoring toolsre scarce. Knowing about weather and moisture danger earlier can help farmers guard crops plan irrigation and choose planting and rotation plans that're better informed. Orbit Crop is a decision‑support tool: its data can be in grids or models and crop fit scores are estimates. Farmers should double‑check Orbit Crops advice with field checks, soil tests and local agricultural specialists.

We made Orbit Crop using Python and FastAPI on the end React and JavaScript on the front end and Tailwind CSS for a flexible interface. Leaflet and OpenStreetMap let users map fields without needing a paid map key. Orbit Crop is a Progressive Web App for phones and computers. To develop or use Orbit Crop you need a web‑ready computer or phone; you do not need farm sensors.

Orbit Crop’s creative idea is to link field mapping NASA Earth‑observation data, crop rotation plans and disaster readiness, in one worldwide tool. The team thought about how much data's available how far the coverage goes how trustworthy the sources are, how to use the tool on a phone how to keep saved alerts when offline and the limits of modeled data. Orbit Crop’s code and the recommendations it creates use SI assistance; the external data still gives credit to the providers.

Due to time restrictions, SI was used to help generate most things on this project except the concepts, ideas and about what features are to be added.
